items.title: Peter LaCaze Interview, 1972-01-27
items.q: I remember one, Arnold Matoia was one. ... He was bright and he played in the band. He played in the white band.

ctx.x: Were there, by the police, me to ask you, were there any mixed bands in the way back when you started?

No, they used to have them like this, but they didn't know it. In other words, if a fellow was colored and he was bright enough to pass, he would play in any band. Because what they wanted, I just told you, they wanted somebody who could do the job. And no matter if he was colored as long as he was bright enough, you know, so it don't make the confusion, well they'll take him. Do you remember? Yeah, I remember one, Arnold Matoia was one. And Dr. Eddie Cherie, Eddie Cherie was one. He was bright and he played in…
They had plenty of others. Yeah, but I didn't know. Yeah, I know, but you know, you'd be surprised. See, all the white musicians knew that.
